newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures end slightly down before key data.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures end slightly down before key data.

text.p: Frozen concentrated orange juice futures closed higher and rangebound ahead of key production reports released Monday.
Most-active July closed up 0.55 cent at 75.40 cents per lb, having ranged from 77.00 to 74.30 cents. The outer contracts ended 1.45 to 0.60 weaker.
Volume was estimated at 2,500 lots compared with Thursday's official 1,093 lots.
Support in July remained at 72.00-70.00 cents, and resistance at 78.00 cents.

The U.S. Department of Agriculture will issue its monthly estimate of the Florida crop at 0830 EDT. No change is expected from the last report, which pegged the crop 221.2 million 90-lb boxes. Yields were seen at 1.57 gallons per box.

Brazil will also release its first official estimate of the new crop on Monday. Market sources expect the estimate to come in around a record 400 million boxes, compared with 364 million boxes produced in 1996/97.
Orange production in the Brazilian state of Sao Paulo is forecast to reach 405 million 40.8 kg boxes in 1997/98, the Brazilian Association of Citrus Exporters (Abecitrus), said today.
Analysts said Monday's bearish report has already been filtered into the market, adding that it is just one of several negative fundamental factors that is expected to keep prices under pressure.
"I don't see how the market could lift its head too high with this oversupply," an analyst said.
The weekly movement figure, meanwhile, remains steady at around 5.3 million gallons.

Merrill Lynch analyst Judith Ganes noted signs of improving demand, including the latest Nielsen data covering retail sales, in a weekly citrus report. She also said Brazilian processors note brisk sales to Europe.
"Even greater demand though, in the U.S. and abroad, will be needed in 1997/98 because of expected increases in supply."
There have been two delivery notices issued to date.
